item.text: {"question_id":"8B.7","answer":"Progress toward Scholz’s frozen goals was mixed, with limited ruler-attributable evidence of net improvement by end-2023. Energy-crisis measures plausibly reduced a worse contraction: DIW modeled a 2.3-percentage-point first-year consumption effect, but estimated only slightly over 0.3% additional consumption and under 0.1% additional GDP, while relief was unevenly distributed—lower-income households benefited more from social and energy transfers, whereas tax relief favored higher-income households somewhat more (BATCH-0034-R12-E003; BATCH-0034-R12-E004; BATCH-0034-R12-E006). These are model estimates covering multi-year measures, and attribution is to the federal government rather than Scholz personally; effects also reflected the mild winter, prior policy, inflation-compensation payments, energy prices, and other actors (BATCH-0034-R12-E001; BATCH-0034-R12-E003; BATCH-0034-R12-E006). Energy supply resilience improved through LNG terminals, storage, and relief according to Scholz’s account, but that account does not independently verify the scale, adequacy, or distribution of the measures (BATCH-0016-E018). Outcomes remained adverse or uneven: GDP fell 0.3%, private consumption 0.8%, and construction investment 2.1%, although equipment investment rose 3.0% and employment reached a record 45.9 million; the macroeconomic figures reflect high prices, interest rates, weak domestic and foreign demand, migration, and inherited or external conditions rather than isolable Scholz effects (BATCH-0028-E001; BATCH-0028-E002; BATCH-0009-E021). Inflation declined from 6.9% in 2022 to 5.9% in 2023, and federal relief partly moderated energy inflation, but food prices rose 12.4%, household energy 14.0%, and core inflation 5.1%; the December comparison was also distorted by the prior year’s one-off gas payment (BATCH-0029-E005). Distributional indicators moved only partly toward protective or egalitarian goals: child poverty risk fell from 15.0% to 14.0%, but 23.9% remained at risk of poverty or social exclusion and the overall poverty-risk rate was 14.4%; these data use prior-year income, cannot be compared with pre-2020 results because of the EU-SILC redesign, and do not identify policy causation (BATCH-0024-E001; BATCH-0024-E002; BATCH-0019-E001). BAföG recipients rose 0.9%, average support 8%, and spending 14%, but school-pupil full funding fell 4% and the data do not show access, unmet need, or educational outcomes; social-assistance spending rose 18%, partly because of the 2022 care-reform baseline, without demonstrating improved welfare (BATCH-0020-E007; BATCH-0020-E006). End-2023 care statistics show 5.7 million people needing care, with the increase partly methodological and demographic and without evidence of service quality or government causation (BATCH-0022-E009). Housing approvals fell 26.6% to the lowest level since 2012, with higher material costs and financing conditions among plausible causes; this is a leading indicator, not completed housing or affordability (BATCH-0023-E001; BATCH-0023-E003). Defense modernization showed little realized progress against inherited deficiencies: readiness problems largely predated Scholz, while the special fund and 2% commitment were judged insufficient, initially slow to spend, and eroded by inflation, interest, and VAT (BATCH-0015-E003; BATCH-0015-E005). The Afghan admission program also lagged—229 selected by June but only 13 admitted by October after a pause—whereas the family-reunification visa quota was met, albeit within a procedurally constrained system (BATCH-0011-R03-E013; BATCH-0011-R06-E006). Overall, crisis containment and some distributional or administrative movement support partial progress, but broad outcome deterioration, uneven distribution, implementation lag, external shocks, inherited constraints, and weak individual attribution prevent a clear net advance across the full portfolio.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0034-R12-E001","BATCH-0034-R12-E003","BATCH-0034-R12-E004","BATCH-0034-R12-E006","BATCH-0016-E018","BATCH-0028-E002","BATCH-0009-E021","BATCH-0029-E005","BATCH-0024-E001","BATCH-0024-E002","BATCH-0019-E001","BATCH-0020-E007","BATCH-0020-E006","BATCH-0022-E009","BATCH-0011-R06-E006"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0028-E001","BATCH-0023-E001","BATCH-0023-E003","BATCH-0015-E003","BATCH-0015-E005","BATCH-0011-R03-E013","BATCH-0034-R12-E006","BATCH-0029-E005"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The frozen-goal portfolio and baseline are not fully reproduced in the supplied passages, so outcome alignment can be assessed only for documented policy areas.","Most causal evidence identifies the federal government or modeled policy effects, not Scholz personally; coalition, state, firm, ECB, migration, and external-shock contributions remain unresolved.","Several indicators have realistic lags, prior-year income references, preliminary or modeled status, methodological breaks, or leading-indicator limitations.","End-2023 evidence cannot establish durable effects on climate modernization, defense readiness, housing completion, educational outcomes, care quality, or long-term poverty."],"corrections_made":["Added the omitted unemployment, inflation, child-poverty, BAföG, social-assistance, and care indicators with their period and methodological limits.","Reduced the positive causal weight assigned to energy relief, wages, and distributional effects by emphasizing model dependence, prior policy, external prices, inflation compensation, and non-Scholz actors.","Clarified that employment, lower child-poverty risk, BAföG growth, and quota fulfillment are outcome signals rather than proof of Scholz-specific causal success.","Retained contrary evidence on macroeconomic contraction, housing, defense implementation, and Afghan admissions while distinguishing inherited deficiencies from new government responsibility."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["Reopen if the full dossier contains a more explicit dated baseline and frozen-goal portfolio for housing, modernization, distribution, defense, and migration.","Reopen if independent evidence isolates Scholz-government effects from coalition, Länder, ECB, market, migration, and external-shock contributions.","Reopen after lagged data become available for housing completions, defense readiness, climate and modernization outcomes, poverty, education, and care quality."]}
